profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 360 Spear Street, San Francisco, CA, per mapping data. This session's fetch of Digital Realty's San Francisco metro property list did not surface a matching named/coded property at this specific address, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building sits within Digital Realty's San Francisco Bay Area footprint, which includes carrier-dense downtown San Francisco buildings and additional sites across the East Bay. Digital Realty markets its Bay Area properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual San Francisco buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage, with the San Francisco Bay Area figuring among the company's longest-held US metros dating back to its original public listing in 2004.

profile.regional_context: The San Francisco Bay Area is one of Digital Realty's longest-standing US colocation markets, anchored by carrier-dense buildings in downtown San Francisco and additional sites across the East Bay. PG&E is the principal electric utility serving most of the region. The Bay Area also hosts large campuses for Google, Meta, and numerous enterprise tenants, some tracked elsewhere in this registry, and its downtown San Francisco buildings, including known carrier hotel locations, are among the most interconnection-dense sites in Digital Realty's North American portfolio.

reading.body:
Digital Realty acquired this 155,000 square foot San Francisco carrier hotel in 2012 for $85 million fully leased, but its current operating status and power capacity remain unconfirmed from the operator's own site.

The building sits in San Francisco's core carrier hotel corridor alongside Digital Realty's 365 Main Street facility, which hosted major web services during a widely documented 2007 power outage. Both properties anchor Digital Realty's Silicon Valley cluster, one of its largest US concentrations. The company does not currently list 360 Spear Street as an individually profiled asset on its public site, making it difficult to establish whether it remains in active operation or what it draws from the regional grid.

This gap reflects a broader data problem: mega-operators like Digital Realty control sprawling portfolios across regions, but do not disclose per-building power consumption or occupancy status for all properties. Trade press captures acquisition events but does not track what happens after. For anyone tracking AI infrastructure buildout, this means carrier hotels in dense urban clusters—which typically serve as expansion points for cloud operators—remain largely invisible once integrated into larger holdings, even when they are material facilities by square footage.
